review_scope: Complete Chinese–English alignment read including both tables, title/deck and retained self-corrections. Ten local corrections recorded; no silent repair of the substantive source conflicts.

changes.before: Putting them side by side is the main move of this volume. Separately each looks like common sense; together it shows that they do not govern the same thing.
changes.after: Only by putting the four side by side do their differences become visible. That comparison is the main move of this volume. Separately each looks like common sense; together it shows that they do not govern the same thing.
changes.reason: Restore the opening methodological step rather than leave it implicit.

changes.before: Kant: vices get carried into the state of peace. The sixth preliminary article forbids assassins, poisoners, breach of capitulation, incitement to treason. He gives six reasons, and the least-quoted is the sixth: these infernal arts, once employed, do not long remain within the limits of war. Take the use of spies — here one merely takes advantage of another's dishonesty; but such vices, once encouraged, cannot in the nature of things be rooted out, and will be carried over into the state of peace, where their presence will utterly destroy the purpose of that state. Note why he names spies. He writes it himself: here one merely takes advantage of another's dishonesty — he knows this is the most harmless-looking of the family, and picks it for exactly that reason. If even this one spills over, the heavier ones need no arguing.
changes.after: Kant: vices get carried into the state of peace. The sixth preliminary article forbids assassins, poisoners, breach of capitulation, incitement to treason. He gives six reasons, and the least-quoted is the sixth: these infernal arts are already base in themselves and, once employed, do not long remain within the limits of war. Take the use of spies — here one merely takes advantage of another's dishonesty; but such vices, once encouraged, cannot in the nature of things be rooted out, and will be carried over into the state of peace, where their presence will utterly destroy the purpose of that state. Note why he names spies. He writes it himself: here one merely takes advantage of another's dishonesty — he knows this is the most harmless-looking of the family, and picks it for exactly that reason. If even this one spills over, the heavier ones need no arguing.
changes.reason: Restore 本身已经卑劣, separate from the later spillover argument.

changes.before: Each one's blind spot can be named. Kant's cannot check the immediate case. A means genuinely used once, genuinely forming no habit, gets no verdict — and only once is a judgement one can sincerely believe in war. Arendt's cannot check means that do not use violence. Deception, bribery, blockade, information manipulation fall outside her definition — and those are the most-used class today. Machiavelli's cannot check the case with no professional body. An army raised for the occasion and disbanded after produces no one who lives by war. SAE's cannot check means that need no information asymmetry. A cruelty conducted in the open, with the executor fully informed, gets no verdict from §12.
changes.after: Each one's blind spot can be named. Kant's cannot check the immediate case. A means genuinely used once, genuinely forming no habit, gets no verdict — and only once is a judgement one can sincerely believe in war. Arendt's cannot check means that do not use violence. Deception, bribery, blockade, information manipulation fall outside her definition — and those are among the most commonly used means today. Machiavelli's cannot check the case with no professional body. An army raised for the occasion and disbanded after produces no one who lives by war. SAE's cannot check means that need no information asymmetry. A cruelty conducted in the open, with the executor fully informed, gets no verdict from §12.
changes.reason: Restore 一类 without making an exclusive top-ranked claim.

changes.before: 1795, the sixth article's sixth reason: the corruption of deceit spills over into the state of peace and destroys the purpose of peace itself. That is a diagnosis — a description of something that will happen. 1797, Doctrine of Right §57: a state under attack may use any means of defence except those that would make its subjects unfit to be citizens, because then it would itself no longer qualify to exist as a person in the relations of states; and the list of prohibitions opens with using one's own subjects as spies. That is already a criterion: it lays down a prohibition and gives the anchor for judging it — the civic standing of one's own subjects.
changes.after: 1795, the sixth article's sixth reason: the corruption of deceit spills over into the state of peace and destroys the purpose of peace itself. That is a diagnosis — a description of something that will happen. 1797, Doctrine of Right §57: a state under attack may use any means of defence except those that would make its subjects unfit to be citizens, because then it would itself no longer qualify to exist as a person under international law in the relations of states; and the list of prohibitions opens with using one's own subjects as spies. That is already a criterion: it lays down a prohibition and gives the anchor for judging it — the civic standing of one's own subjects.
changes.reason: Restore 按国际法, as in the matching Kant passage in if01.

changes.reason: Restore the actual named heading, not a replacement drawn from the following paragraph.

changes.before: Five trigger questions go with it; any one of them hit means a candidate ground conflict is registered first, and only then may one explain why it is not one. Does it fold a particular person into the overall interest of a family, a state, an undertaking or a community? Does it abolish his independent position to refuse, to withdraw, to revise, to answer, or to reorganize himself? Is he used merely as a means — that is, does his own standing as an end fail to enter consideration in this arrangement? (Replaceability is an external indicator of this one, not its definition: an irreplaceable person can equally be used merely as a means.) Does an external purpose acquire authorisation to abolish his position as a subject? Is consent, willingness, honour, duty or community membership treated as an automatic exemption from the prohibition on merely as a means?
changes.after: Five trigger questions go with it; any one of them hit means a candidate ground conflict is registered first, and only then may one explain why it is not one. Does it fold a particular person into the overall interest of a family, a state, an undertaking or a community? Does it abolish his independent position to refuse, to withdraw, to revise, to answer, or to reorganize himself? Is he used merely as a means — that is, does his own standing as an end fail to enter consideration in this arrangement? (Replaceability is an external indicator of this one, not its definition: an irreplaceable person can equally be used merely as a means.) Is authorisation to abolish his position as a subject obtained from an external purpose? Is consent, willingness, honour, duty or community membership treated as an automatic exemption from the prohibition on merely as a means?
changes.reason: Restore the direction of authorisation: the arrangement claims authority from the external purpose, rather than that purpose receiving authority.

changes.before: Wartime secrecy — the first question asks about depth. Secrecy to the point where the executor cannot judge what he is doing: fails. Secrecy that merely withholds times and places from the enemy: passes. This cell could not be judged before; with the four questions it can, because the first question breaks the vague word secrecy into a specific question about the executor.
changes.after: Wartime secrecy — the first question asks about depth. Secrecy to the point where the executor cannot judge what he is doing: fails. Secrecy that merely withholds times and places from outsiders: passes. This cell could not be judged before; with the four questions it can, because the first question breaks the vague word secrecy into a specific question about the executor.

changes.before: The evidence is in one and the same book. In The Art of War Machiavelli gives the fullest version of this mechanism there is — six reasons, from livelihood to incentive to constitutional trilemma, written out layer by layer. And in chapter five of The Prince he argues for destroying a city accustomed to freedom. The two do not contradict, because they answer different questions: the first asks how a republic should arrange its internal affairs, the second how to hold a newly conquered city. He is self-consistent in both.
changes.after: The evidence is in one and the same book. In The Art of War Machiavelli gives one of the fullest versions of this mechanism — six reasons, from livelihood to incentive to constitutional trilemma, written out layer by layer. And in chapter five of The Prince he argues for destroying a city accustomed to freedom. The two do not contradict, because they answer different questions: the first asks how a republic should arrange its internal affairs, the second how to hold a newly conquered city. He is self-consistent in both.
changes.reason: Restore 最完整的一个 rather than an exclusive superlative.

changes.before: §12's criterion is bound to the single variable of information asymmetry, and the substitution case is a counter-example — everyone informed, position abolished. Whether §12 needs a supplementary criterion independent of information asymmetry is undecided. The candidate — a fifth derived check, is the executor in a position to refuse — already has a concrete test object, and it stops that case. Its standing must be written down: it is a derived check, not a substitute for the gate on the ground. A man able to refuse and not refusing may still be used merely as a means, so the gate can under no circumstances be replaced by it.
changes.after: §12's criterion is bound to the single variable of information asymmetry, and the substitution case is a counter-example — everyone informed, position abolished. Whether §12 needs a supplementary criterion independent of information asymmetry is undecided. The candidate — a fifth derived check beyond the four, is the executor in a position to refuse — already has a concrete test object, and it stops that case. Its standing must be written down: it is a derived check, not a substitute for the gate on the ground. A man able to refuse and not refusing may still be used merely as a means, so the gate can under no circumstances be replaced by it.
changes.reason: Restore 四问之外 explicitly, retaining its subordinate status relative to the ground gate.

unresolved_source_questions.finding: The substitution involves beheading, but the claim of passing all four screens rests partly on no violence. The fourth screen is actually about replacing concerted action, not simply presence of violence. Need an author-defined test object and proof; cannot certify the all-four-passed inference.
Cross-reference to a complete treatment of The Prince chapter5 in volume2 is not supported by a full read of frozen if02; no such treatment appears there.
One and the same book is contradicted immediately by references to two separate books.
